title: OpenAI Wants to Put ChatGPT in Your Glasses: Brockman Eyes Wearable API, Still in Early Prototype

content_html:
Greg Brockman, CEO of OpenAI, recently pointed the company's next steps towards the human body during a conversation with journalists in New York. He stated that OpenAI is very interested in integrating ChatGPT and related AI capabilities into wearable devices, especially products like smart glasses. "We are definitely very interested in integration," he said, "I think this is a use case for APIs — to spread it out so anyone can do the integration."

Brockman revealed that OpenAI is considering opening access through APIs to third-party devices, allowing hardware such as smart glasses to utilize voice interaction capabilities similar to ChatGPT Live. In his view, this should become an interface for interaction and be available on all devices. However, he also admitted that the relevant API is still in a very early stage and has a long way to go before it is fully developed.

Currently, some smart glasses on the market (such as Rokid's products) can call upon OpenAI's models, but that is not a complete account-level access to ChatGPT. Manufacturers such as Meta, Google, and Samsung are also accelerating their own AI glasses projects. Brockman mentioned that OpenAI hopes to allow users in the future to directly use tools such as ChatGPT or Codex through wearable devices, achieving more comprehensive control than within a mobile application, rather than being limited to the restricted interactions on a screen.

As for OpenAI's own hardware plans, Brockman only mentioned that the direction may differ from existing wearable devices, revealing no specific details. He emphasized that broader device integration requires support from new APIs — wearable devices have special needs for running continuously in the background and processing multi-modal inputs such as cameras. This kind of integration is categorized by him as part of OpenAI's long-term vision, but for now, it still stands at the threshold of exploration.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 最近在纽约与记者交谈时指出了该公司在人体方面的下一步举措。 他表示，OpenAI非常有兴趣将ChatGPT和相关AI能力集成到可穿戴设备中，特别是智能眼镜等产品中。 “我们绝对对集成非常感兴趣，”他说，“我认为这是 API 的一个用例——将其传播出去，这样任何人都可以进行集成。”

Brockman透露，OpenAI正在考虑通过API向第三方设备开放访问，让智能眼镜等硬件能够利用类似于ChatGPT Live的语音交互功能。 在他看来，这应该成为一个交互的界面，并且在所有设备上都可用。 不过，他也承认，相关API仍处于非常早期的阶段，距离完全开发还有很长的路要走。

目前，市场上的一些智能眼镜（例如Rokid的产品）可以调用OpenAI的模型，但这并不是完整的帐户级访问ChatGPT。 Meta、谷歌、三星等厂商也在加速自己的AI眼镜项目。 Brockman提到，OpenAI希望未来让用户通过可穿戴设备直接使用ChatGPT或Codex等工具，实现比移动应用程序内更全面的控制，而不是局限于屏幕上的受限交互。

至于OpenAI自己的硬件计划，布罗克曼只提到方向可能与现有的可穿戴设备有所不同，没有透露具体细节。 他强调，更广泛的设备集成需要新 API 的支持——可穿戴设备对于在后台持续运行和处理摄像头等多模式输入有特殊的需求。 这种整合被他归类为OpenAI长期愿景的一部分，但目前还处于探索的门槛。
